[PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
## Consolidated Experience from Similar Tasks
To move an object to a target surface: first locate the object and the target destination. Before attempting pick_up, navigate to the object and ensure it is within reachable grasping range, because a pick action will fail if the robot is not near the object. After pick_up, explicitly verify that the robot is actually holding the object. Before attempting put_down, verify that the robot is still holding the object; a place action is invalid if the robot is not holding anything. If the named target surface instance is unavailable, explore other instances or retry rather than stopping. Then navigate to the target surface and execute put_down. Success is indicated by successful find and pick_up of the object, successful find of the target surface, and a final successful put_down.

## Preliminary Thinking
1. Locate a pear item; if there are multiple pears, choose one that is reachable. 2. Navigate to that pear. 3. Execute pick_up for the pear and verify that the robot is holding it. 4. Locate the indicated sofa; if the specific sofa cannot be found, search other sofa instances or retry until a valid indicated target is found. 5. Navigate to the sofa while holding the pear. 6. Execute put_down to place the pear on the sofa. 7. Verify that the pear is successfully placed on the target sofa.
[/PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
